Package com.example.thevms.model

Class Event

java.lang.Object
com.example.thevms.model.Event
public class Event extends Object
Represents an event Object.

Creation Workflow:

  1. Call the static create(String, String, Organizer, String, byte[], Date, Date, Date, Date, boolean, Double, Location, boolean) method.
  2. This method asynchronously fetches a unique ID from the database.
  3. It then returns a Task<Event>. You use an .addOnSuccessListener to get the in-memory Event object.
  4. The created object does NOT yet exist in the database.

Saving and Updating:

  • To save the event to the database for the first time, or to update it after making changes, you MUST call the save() method.
  • The save() method is also asynchronous and returns a Task<Void> that you can listen to for success or failure.

Example Usage: 

 
 // 1. Create the event in memory (gets a unique ID async)
 Event.create(name, desc, org, loc, imgUrl, date, date, date, date, geolocationRequired, radius, geoLocation, isPrivate)
      .addOnSuccessListener(event -> {
          // 2. Save the event to the database
          event.save()
               .addOnSuccessListener(aVoid -> {
                   // Success!
               });
               .addOnFailureListener(e -> {
                   // Error!
               });
      });

  • Method Details

    • create

      public static com.google.android.gms.tasks.Task<Event> create(String name, String description, Organizer organizer, String location, byte[] photo, Date registrationStartTime, Date registrationEndTime, Date eventStartTime, Date eventEndTime, boolean geolocationRequired, Double radius, android.location.Location geoLocation, boolean isPrivate)
      Asynchronously creates an Event object in memory with a unique ID from the database.

      This method is the designated factory for creating new Event instances. It first makes a network call to the database to secure a new, unique eventId. Only after the ID is successfully retrieved does it construct the Event object in memory.

      Important: This method only creates the object locally. It does NOT save it to the database. You must call the save() method on the returned object to persist it.

      Parameters:
      name - Name of the event.
      description - Description of the event.
      organizer - The event organizer.
      location - The event location.
      photo - The event's poster image as raw bytes.
      registrationStartTime - The start time for registration.
      registrationEndTime - The end time for registration.
      eventStartTime - The start time of the event.
      eventEndTime - The end time of the event.
      geolocationRequired - Boolean flag for geofencing.
      radius - The radius limit for joining (in km).
      geoLocation - The Location object containing coordinates.
      isPrivate - Boolean flag for event privacy.
      Returns:
      A Task<Event> that, upon completion, will contain the fully initialized Event object.
